tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). A card the user answered has already left, "Do it here" included, so it needs no call.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__hand_off_to_session
tools.description: Move the task you are in the middle of into its own session (a fork of this conversation plus your remaining plan) so you can answer the user now. Use it when a new user message about something else arrives mid-task — not for small corrections or when the user said to keep the work here. In a worktree the fork gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip: commit first (uncommitted edits stay here). Bold title line and one sentence right before the call; after it, stop that task here and answer the new message — no recap.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

action.description: What to do. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). #!/bin/bash
# usage: axcheck.sh Module.Name [Module.Name ...]   (run after lake build of those modules)
SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref
F=$SP/axcheck_$$.lean
{
  echo "import Lean"
  for m in "$@"; do echo "import $m"; done
  echo 'open Lean Elab Command in'
  echo '#eval show Lean.Core.CoreM Unit from do'
  echo '  let env ← getEnv'
  printf '  for modName in [%s] do\n' "$(printf '`%s, ' "$@" | sed 's/, $//')"
  cat <<'L'
    let some mod := env.getModuleIdx? modName | throwError "no module"
    let mut all := 0
    let mut thms := 0
    let mut bad : Array (Name × Array Name) := #[]
    for (n, ci) in env.constants.map₁.toList do
      if env.getModuleIdxFor? n == some mod then
        all := all + 1
        if let .thmInfo _ := ci then thms := thms + 1
        let axs ← collectAxioms n
        let extra := axs.filter fun a => a != ``propext && a != ``Quot.sound
        if !extra.isEmpty then bad := bad.push (n, extra)
    IO.println s!"{modName}: constants {all}, theorems {thms}"
    IO.println s!"outside propext, Quot.sound: {bad}"
L
} > $F
cd /Users/guygouri/Devlab/ernlang/ern/formal && ~/.elan/bin/lake env lean $F
rm -f $F
----

# User arbitrations of the blocking report (verbatim, French)

Arbitrages (rapport bloquant, section 7) :

Q1 : (b). Ajouter à §63 « la destination est utilisable dans l'état d'arrivée ».
Q2 : lecture mixte sur l'état d'arrivée : invariants du noyau sur l'état entier, plus ArenaInv de la nouvelle entrée ; NewArenaBase porte cette lecture.
Q3 : réalisation par des pas du noyau. freeSlot (contrat HandlePool v0.5) marque l'entrée libre et incrémente la génération ; préconditions : droit d'administration, pool vivant, handle valide, aucune feuille de l'entrée à Init (Uninit ou Moved), aucune autorité active dérivée d'une compagne de ce pool sur l'entrée ; aucun effet d'endUse. Deux preuves obligatoires :
  (1) témoin complet depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés : newPool, allocSlot, resolve Modify, écriture, transfer de la valeur vers un local de même forme, unresolve, freeSlot accepté ;
  (2) la mise à jour des métadonnées (état libre, génération) est réalisable par une écriture autorisée sous le droit d'administration.
Q4 : garantie par pool : réécrire D.2, D.3 et D.4(3) sur les compagnes du pool du slot ; les pools imbriqués restent permis ; I1 et les garanties du noyau restent prouvées sur l'état entier.
Q5 : la validation du handle précède le contrôle du droit : fail dans les deux cas.
Q6 : réécrire §86 s4 : « La réémission ne modifie ni les octets ni l'état d'initialisation. Une lecture reste soumise aux conditions ordinaires du modèle mémoire, notamment Init, aux droits d'accès et à la validité de représentation pour le type demandé. La Spec 4 déterminera les obligations de construction et de typage des valeurs réémises. »
Q7 : restreindre §78.3 aux ancres du sous-arbre strict de internal qui couvrent une feuille du stockage administré ; prouver que la clause découle de §78.2 et de I3 (lecture Q9), et l'équivalence de reset avec sa séquence du noyau dans les deux sens.
Q8 : ajouter à §47 : le graphe de possession des statiques est acyclique.
Q9 et Q26 : « valide » = active. §69.2 : endUse est rejeté si une autorité détenue par place a un descendant actif détenu ailleurs.
Q10 : (a).
Q11 : (a) fail ; (b) reject ; (c) reject ; (d) mark exige AdminRight ; (e) grow suit le détenteur actuel du bloc ; (f) fail avant le contrôle du droit (contrat DS-v2).
Q12 : avec le nouveau freeSlot, un handle d'entrée libre est périmé : fail.
Q13 : §71.2 inchangé ; préciser au §36 que MetaRight vise la création ou le recyclage d'autorités sur un stockage existant, pas la création d'une allocation fraîche par alloc ; la concurrence entre appels relève de la spec 2.
Q14 : « opérations d'accès » = O9–O11 ; le préciser au §59.
Q15 : restreindre §40 aux emplacements racines utilisables, comme §49.7.
Q16 : définir I5 : toute feuille épinglée appartient à un emplacement utilisable.
Q17 : lecture actuelle.
Q18 : région dont toutes les feuilles sont de taille nulle : base et provenance de l'allocation de l'ancre effective, comme la région vide.
Q19 : H31a : le jumeau à plusieurs pas (conjonct 5) est accepté.
Q20 : non bloquants (classés).
Q21 : pour chaque cas dont le verdict attendu change, conserver le verdict historique, sa justification et le nouveau verdict fondé sur la v0.1 (tableau dans la description de PR) :
  - H21, H50, H51 : nouveau verdict = verdict obtenu ;
  - H49 : conservé comme test de régression, verdict = verdict obtenu, blocage résiduel documenté (décision NoLock) ; exception explicite : le reset rejeté de H49 est dispensé de jumeau positif ;
  - H16 classé spec 3 ; W2 et W3 : les variantes deviennent les cas ; MM2-H H01 : la variante devient le jumeau ; H10 : l'accès sort de l'allocation ; W1 : la valeur est retirée avant freeSlot.
Q22 : non bloquants (frontières ouvertes de la spec) ; exitRoots retenu comme réalisation de référence.
Q23 : lectures dont un témoin du rapport change un verdict :
  - B#1, B#15, B#33, SP-A4, machine S1 et S2 : lectures actuelles conservées (B#15 imposée par Q9) ;
  - B#28 : remplacée par Q9 ;
  - B#45 : remplacée : chaque pin crée une obligation d'épinglage d'identité fraîche ; une feuille est épinglée tant qu'une obligation active la couvre ; unpin désigne une obligation et ne lève qu'elle ; K.ExternalDone porte sur cette obligation ;
  - H-R5 : sans objet ; DS-R1 à DS-R13 : tranchées par Q11, Q27 et Q28.
  Les lectures sans témoin de différence sont conservées.
Q24 : le fournisseur doit être un emplacement utilisable (§71.2).
Q25 : (b).
Q27 : (a).
Q28 : (c) fail (une pile morte invalide ses marques).

Spec : ne pas modifier `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`. Créer `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` à partir de la v0, avec les amendements Q1, Q2, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q9/Q26, Q13, Q14, Q15, Q16, Q18, Q24 et B#45 (§74, §75), en anglais ; en-tête : « Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated », suivi de la liste des clauses modifiées. Commit séparé `docs(specs): add memory model v0.1 corrective candidate`. La reconstruction suit la v0.1.
Contrats locaux : HandlePool v0.5 (Q3, Q4, Q5, Q12) et DS-v2 (Q11, Q27, Q28), changements listés dans la description de PR.
Preuves : refaire celles qui sont touchées ; les garanties de Q1, Q3, Q7 et B#45 sont démontrées sur les états atteignables du contrat, sans hypothèse supplémentaire non normative ; tout échec de preuve est rapporté, jamais contourné. Ouvrir la PR si la condition du brief est remplie.

## Follow-up answers (verbatim, French)

Q9 (suite) : règle unifiée. endUse et free sont rejetés si une autorité qu'ils désactivent — détenue par un emplacement qui meurt, stockage possédé transitivement compris, ou racine d'un stockage libéré — a un descendant actif, quelle que soit son empreinte, que le même pas ne désactive pas. Les cas (1) et (2) sont donc rejetés. La sortie de cadre garde son ré-ancrage, et rejette si aucune origine survivante n'existe (inchangé). I2 au sens « origine active » tient après chaque pas.

Q3 (suite) : remplace Q17. Dans §63.4, §69.2 et §70.3, sont exemptées des contrôles « autorité dérivée active couvrant depuis l'extérieur » les autorités par lesquelles le pas exerce son droit Modify : l'autorité exerçable qui fonde le droit et sa chaîne d'origines (pour le pool : entrée, compagne, internal et ses origines). Les autres autorités actives restent contrôlées. Le témoin Q3 (1) devient : resolve Modify, écriture, transfer de l'entrée vers un local, unresolve, freeSlot accepté, y compris avec internal dérivé. W1 suit le même chemin. Réévaluer W2 sous cette lecture. Ajouter §63.4, §69.2 et §70.3 aux amendements de la v0.1.

(Cases (1) and (2) above refer to: (1) endUse(p) where p owns an allocation q holding a stored authority a, the frame holding b derived from a over another static; (2) free(p) with an empty-footprint derivative of p's root held by the frame.)

## Second follow-up answers (verbatim, French), after the library phase

HandlePool v0.5, freeSlot : remplacer la condition par « aucune autorité active, descendante stricte de internal de ce pool, ne couvre l'entrée ». Le ré-ancrage sur internal (§73) est alors couvert, et la garantie reste par pool : un pool imbriqué dans une entrée bloque la libération de cette entrée, alors que les autorités du pool parent ne bloquent pas les freeSlot du pool imbriqué, puisqu'elles sont des ancêtres de son internal et non des descendantes. pool_no_stale_access doit tenir sous cette règle.

DataStack :
- DS-R1 : toute cellule de position ≥ m.top (lecture la plus stricte) ;
- DS-R4 : grow avec extra = 0 est ok (réémission en place de la même région) ;
- DS-R3 : rewind sur un indice de pile inexistant donne fail, comme une marque invalide (cohérent avec Q5 et Q28).

Q5 : oui, étendre à freeSlot. La validation du handle précède le contrôle du droit : le handle d'un pool mort donne fail.

/-- Base of `pool_two_freeSlot_cross` (§72, §71, §60, §65; HandlePool v0.5, D.1): frame 1 with
the allocator 0, the pool value 1 and the leaves 2, 3, 4; storage 5 (entries 6, 7) owned by 1,
pool 0 on it with `internal` its root 5; then 6, `Modify` on the whole storage from 5, stored into
the leaf 4. -/
def pxo : List COp := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1],
  .alloc 0 1 [lf, pt 5, pt 5], .newPool 5 5, .derive 5 [6, 7] .modify, .store 6 4]
/-- State reached by `pxo` (§57). -/
def px : CState := cfinal K0 [] pxo
/-- The twin of `pool_two_freeSlot_cross` continued as the draft witness, up to its `freeSlot`:
pool 1 on `internal` 6 over the same storage; slot 0 allocated in each pool (the place 6 in both);
the leaf 6 written through 6. -/

# v0.1 reconstruction: library brief (HandlePool v0.5, DataStack DS-v2)

Read first: `SP/v01/kernel-brief.md` (context, hard rules, kernel design), `SP/v01/arena-ref-brief.md`
(arena changes, notably `NewArenaBase` now carrying v0.1 §76.6), `SP/v01/arbitration.md` (Q3, Q4, Q5,
Q11, Q12, Q21 W1, Q23, Q27, Q28 and the two follow-up answers), and the reports in
`SP/v01/kernel-report.md` and `SP/v01/arena-report.md`.
`SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref`.

Both contracts are local, non-normative library contracts. Docstrings cite the applicable spec
clauses (v0.1) and the contract identifier: "HandlePool v0.5" or "DS-v2", stated as non-normative.
Agents H (`formal/Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean`) and D (`formal/Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean`) run in parallel:
never run `lake build`; check with `cd formal && ~/.elan/bin/lake env lean Ern/Lib/<File>.lean`.
Do not touch corpus files (the corpus phase follows).

## HandlePool v0.5 = HandlePool v0.4 annex (Annex D of `~/Downloads/ERN_MM-03.3_v0.4_pour_validation.md`, lines 687–725) with these changes

- HP5-1 `freeSlot` (Q3). Preconditions: administration right (`AdminRight`: live pool, `MetaRight` =
  `Modify` exercisable on the pool value, §36); valid handle; no leaf of the entry is `Init` (each is
  `Uninit` or `Moved`); no active authority derived from a companion of this pool (a strict
  descendant of a companion recorded for this pool) covers a leaf of the entry. Effect: the slot
  becomes free and its generation is incremented; NO end-of-use effect: the kernel state is unchanged.
  Outcome order: keep the existing order of `FreeSlotStep` (`reject` without pool or right, then `fail`
  on an invalid handle, then `reject` on the content conditions); Q5 concerns resolution (§89) and is
  not extended to `freeSlot` (report this as a point for the user).
  Remove what only served the v0.4 `freeSlot`: `Exempt`, `DyingAccessOK`, `ContentAnchorOK`,
  `ContentEndPre`, `contentEnd_*`, `freeSlot_preserves*` on `endUseEff`, `freeSlot_lands_in_reachable`
  and the HP-4 step-level discussion (moot: no kernel effect), and the v0.4 obligation
  `pool_freeSlot_ends_content`.
- HP5-2 Mandatory proof (1) (Q3, follow-up): a complete witness from `PState.init statics` by accepted
  steps: `newPool`, `allocSlot`, `resolve` in `Modify`, a write of the entry through the resolved entry
  authority (kernel `write`), `transfer` of the entry's value to a local of the same shape, `unresolve`,
  then `freeSlot` accepted. `internal` must be DERIVED (as in the corpus pools: derived from the
  storage root and stored in the pool value). The transfer relies on the v0.1 §63.4 exemption (the
  entry, the companion, `internal` and its origins ground the right). "Local": prefer a place created
  by `enterFrame` (§72) owned by the current frame; if that is infeasible in the run, use a static
  `Uninit` place directly owned by frame 0 and say why in the docstring and report.
- HP5-3 Mandatory proof (2) (Q3): the metadata update of `freeSlot` (free state, generation) is
  realizable by an authorized write under the administration right: for every library-reachable state
  and pool with `AdminRight`, the kernel `write` (§67, `Write3Pre`) of the leaves of the pool value

HasRight / ExercisableAt (§43): one authority exercisable at m with sufficient effective mode on every leaf (∃ a, ∀ l) as the draft -> recorded.

Well-formedness of the statics declaration (acyclic ownership, parents before children) is not stated by §47: keep the draft ShapeOK-style hypothesis as a hypothesis of the init theorems and record it as a spec gap.

python3 -I - <<'EOF'
import re,glob,collections
spec=open('specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md').read()
norm=lambda s:re.sub(r'\s+',' ',s.replace('`','')).strip()
specn=norm(spec)
res=collections.defaultdict(list)
for f in sorted(glob.glob('formal/Ern/**/*.lean',recursive=True)):
    txt=open(f).read()
    # comments only
    for m in re.finditer(r'/-.*?-/',txt,re.S):
        c=m.group(0)
        for q in re.finditer(r'"([^"]{25,})"',c,re.S):
            s=norm(q.group(1))
            line=txt[:m.start()+q.start()].count('\n')+1
            inspec = s in specn
            res[f].append((line,inspec,len(s),s[:110]))
tot=0
for f,l in res.items():
    ins=[x for x in l if x[1]]
    print(f, 'quotes>=25ch:',len(l),'verbatim-in-spec:',len(ins), 'chars-in-spec:',sum(x[2] for x in ins))
    tot+=len(ins)
print('total verbatim spec quotes',tot)

EOF

content.content:
# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.
- §40: `RootHeld` restricted to usable root places, as in §49.7; the two clauses differed on unusable root places.
- §47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; a static ownership cycle made §57 false in the initial state.
- §51: a valid origin is an active origin; "valid" was undefined there.
- §57: definition of I5, which v0 named without defining.
- §59: "access operations" are O9–O11; read as all operations, §59 contradicted §69.
- §60.1: a valid origin chain is an active one, read through §44.
- §63.4: the active derived authorities covering the source from outside are named, and the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right are exempt; without this exemption no value could be moved through a derived authority.
- §63.9 (new): the destination is usable in the resulting state; without it an accepted transfer could create an ownership cycle and break §49.8 and §57.
- §69.2 and §70.3: the same exemption as §63.4, and rejection when an authority made inactive by the step keeps an active descendant; without it an accepted step left an active authority with an inactive origin.
- §71.2: the provider is a usable place; v0 did not require it to exist.
- §74 and §75: each `pin` installs an obligation of fresh identity and `unpin` ends one designated obligation; per-leaf pin flags let an `unpin` lift a pin installed by another `pin`.
- §76.6: the reading of the precondition (whole kernel state, `ArenaInv` of the new entry, resulting state); v0 admitted several readings with different verdicts.
- §78.3: restricted to anchors covering a leaf of the administered storage; as written, its second sentence was false.
- §82.2: address and provenance of a pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size; v0 decided no address for that region.
- §86: the last sentence is rewritten; as written, it was false, since `reset` and `issue` leave a recycled leaf `Init` and readable.

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

## Validation and Revision Procedure

This edition has been validated and acquires normative authority under the ERN Charter v0. Any subsequent semantic change must identify the clauses concerned, justify the change, and preserve the guarantees of the ERN Charter v0. Formal models and proofs are instruments for verifying this specification, not sources of additional rules. Behaviors not determined within its scope are explicitly identified.

## Scope

This specification defines:

- the safe-code contract;
- the abstract machine for allocations, bytes, and accesses;
- the second-class access discipline;
- footprints, authorities, dependencies, frames, and ownership;
- read, write, transfer, release, allocation, and pinning transitions;
- the normative contract of arenas as a reference library abstraction;
/-!
# Elementary memory machine (spec v0, Parts II–III, §8–§20)

Source: `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`. Citations: `§N.k` is numbered item `k`
of section `N`; `§N ¶p` is the `p`-th paragraph of section `N`, a list belonging to the
paragraph that introduces it.

* State, allocations, bytes, places and accesses (§9–§12).
* Effects of valid operations: `State.write`, `State.dealloc`, `State.alloc`.
* Raw operations as transition relations with `ok`/`ub` outcomes, stated on every state
  (§20.1): `ReadStep`, `WriteStep`, `DeallocStep`, `AllocStep`. Typed reads and writes carry
  a type argument of an opaque type `Ty`; their unspecified obligations are explicit
  parameters split into a decidable part `dec` and a static part `stat` (§20.3).
* Interpreters `read`, `write`, `dealloc`, `alloc`, computable, with the static part as a
  proof argument (§20.3 ¶3), agreeing with the relations in both directions.
* Executions `Exec` (sequences of `ok` steps) from any initial state (§9 ¶9).
-/

# Handle pool: a library instance of the access discipline (non-normative)

**Non-normative.** This module formalizes the library contract "HandlePool v0.5": the HandlePool
v0.4 annex (items D.1–D.4) as amended by the arbitrations Q3, Q4, Q5 and Q12 (items HP5-1 to
HP5-7) and by the second follow-up to Q3 and Q5 (HP5-1', HP5-1''). `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` does not define it (Part XIV preamble: "The
contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined
here"). The normative clauses that constrain it are §36 (`MetaRight` is exercisable `Modify` on the
administering value; `writeShared` alone is insufficient; the library adds no rights to the
kernel), §37 and §89 (handles are data, not authorities; a stale identity or generation leads to
defined failure), §38 and §46 (library state outside `S₃`), §47 (empty initial registry), §56 (the
guard over all registries of live administrations), §58 (outcomes) and §76 (the obligations of
`newArena` that `newPool` takes over).

The pool registry lives beside the kernel state (`PState`). Its operations are built on the
kernel operations O1–O16 (§60–§75): `newPool` registers only; `allocSlot` writes the handle into
its destination (O10); `resolve` derives a companion from `internal` over the whole storage, then
an entry authority from the companion (O1 twice); `resolveMany` does the same with `split` (O2) in
`Modify` and with one `Observe` derive per handle (O1) in `Observe`; `unresolve` releases (O3);
`freeSlot` updates the registry only (HP5-1). Every library step is thus, on the kernel side, a
finite sequence of accepted kernel steps (`pstep_kernel`), so, under `DDSound` (§80) and
`StaticsOK` (§47), every kernel state of a library run is kernel-reachable and satisfies the
invariant of §57 (`kernel_guarantee`, HP5-7).
-/

--- 0f35854 Guy Senpai <guy.senpai@gmail.com>
test(corpus): replay the HandlePool and DataStack cases on v0.5 and DS-v2

The library runner follows HandlePool v0.5 (freeSlot without kernel
effect, handle checked before the right) and DS-v2. Where an expected
verdict changes, the docstring keeps the historical verdict, its
justification and the new verdict derived from the contract or v0.1
text: H31a, pool_free_entry_handle and pool_dead now fail; the cross
freeSlot after a write and W1's historical freeSlot are rejected (Init
content); W1 follows the arbitrated path (resolve Modify, write,
transfer to a local, unresolve, freeSlot accepted); W2's variant is
accepted under the §63.4 exemption; DS03 and DS05 are decided by DS-v2.
No mismatch remains. The full lake build succeeds without warnings;
axioms within propext and Quot.sound.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M6R8ERV9702S7XPQBF8E5PHV

--- e278eaf Guy Senpai <guy.senpai@gmail.com>
fix(lib): apply the DS-R1, DS-R3 and DS-R4 decisions to DataStack

As arbitrated for DS-v2: rewind rejects if an active authority derived
from internal covers any cell at a position at or above the mark;
grow with extra = 0 is accepted as an in-place reissue of the same
region; rewind on a missing stack index fails like an invalid mark.
The reading witnesses are now DS-v2 examples, and the O6 theorems,
rewind_ok_iff and RewindStep.det are re-proved (grow_same_base loses
its 0 < extra conjunct, which DS-v2 makes false). DataStack builds
without warnings; axioms within propext and Quot.sound.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M6R60FDXJ1JTSN1PP9QHFM81

--- 6b7e2e1 Guy Senpai <guy.senpai@gmail.com>
fix(lib): block freeSlot on strict descendants of the pool's internal

Under the first v0.5 condition (no active descendant of a companion on
the entry), exitFrame could reanchor a surviving entry authority onto
internal, so freeSlot was accepted while that authority stayed active
and pool_no_stale_access was false (Witness.no_stale_after_exit). As
arbitrated, freeSlot now rejects while an active strict descendant of
the pool's internal covers the entry, and checks the handle, pool
liveness included, before the administration right.

pool_no_stale_access and pool_inv_preserved are proved on every
library-reachable state, through the auxiliary ResAnc. The former
witness now shows the freeSlot rejected. A pool nested in an entry
blocks the freeing of that entry; the parent pool's authorities do not
block the nested pool. HandlePool builds without warnings; axioms
within propext and Quot.sound.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M6R608BAYJS42G88S9GH4KQQ

--- e61da9e Guy Senpai <guy.senpai@gmail.com>
test(corpus): replay MM3-H and MM23-H on spec v0.1

The runner takes unpin on an obligation identity. Every MM3-H and
MM23-H case was rechecked against the amended clauses. Where v0.1 or
the arbitration changes an expected verdict, the docstring keeps the
historical verdict, its justification and the new verdict derived from
the v0.1 text: H16 (accepted reception under the §63.4 exemption, class
Spec 3), H21, H50, H51 (verdict = obtained), H49 (regression test, its
endUse steps now rejected by §69.2, reset exempt from a twin), W3 (the
variant is the case), H26 (unpin of the obligation). MM23-H15 and H16
pass; H14 and H17 are classified. No mismatch remains. The four corpus
modules build without warnings; axioms within propext and Quot.sound.

mark needs the administration right, grow stores the new block into the
place that currently holds the block, and a mark of a dead stack fails

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M6R2H8ETWMKZ017B90K5QGZ5

--- 3f9235b Guy Senpai <guy.senpai@gmail.com>
feat(lib): rebuild HandlePool as the v0.5 contract on spec v0.1

freeSlot needs the administration right, a valid handle, no Init leaf
in the entry and no active descendant of a companion of the pool on it;
it frees the slot and increments the generation without changing the
kernel. resolve checks the handle, pool liveness included, before the
right. Guarantees are per pool, and every library step's kernel effect
is a sequence of accepted kernel steps, so kernel_guarantee needs only
DDSound and StaticsOK. The Q3 witness reaches an accepted freeSlot from
the initial state with a derived internal, and the metadata update is
an authorized write under the administration right.

Open: pool_no_stale_access is false under the current-chain reading of
the companion condition (Witness.no_stale_after_exit); it awaits the
contract owner's arbitration. HandlePool builds without warnings;
axioms within propext and Quot.sound.

{p : Nat} (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2) (h : UnpinStep k p s3 (.ok s3')) : Repr L rtok s3' s2 := by
  obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h

/-- Realization of `endUse` (§82.5, §69: "The operation does not automatically trigger physical
deallocation in the elementary memory machine"): no raw operation; the allocations of the storage
that dies stay live (a leak, which §69 does not prohibit); `Repr` holds after the step. -/
theorem r6_endUse {k : K} {L : Layout} {rtok : Nat → Nat} {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : Machine.State}
of the root places directly owned by the exiting frame are `ok` raw steps, those allocations are
dead afterwards, and `Repr` holds after the step. The storage owned by those places is not
deallocated (§73: "Exiting does not entail automatic physical deallocation of all dead
places"). -/
theorem r6_exit {Ty : Type} {k : K} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {L : Layout} {rtok : Nat → Nat} {s3 s3' : S3}
/-- v0.1 §86, example: a reissued leaf keeps its initialization state and a read of it remains
subject to the ordinary conditions of the memory model. Leaf 1 is `Uninit` when it is first issued,
is written through block 4, keeps `Init` across `endUse` of the destination, the legal `reset`
(§78: "No leaf is made `Init` by `reset`") and the reissue, which modifies the initialization state
of no leaf of the region (§86, `issue_keeps_init`) and initializes only the destination 2 (§77).
